title: [Refurb] Sangean Clock Radio DAB+/FM-RDS Digital Dual Alarm-DCR-89+ $39.99 Shipped @ The Wicked Yak Clearance Center eBay
body:
Deal: [Refurb] Sangean Clock Radio DAB+/FM-RDS Digital Dual Alarm-DCR-89+ $39.99 Shipped @ The Wicked Yak Clearance Center eBay

[carrawa] So, what was the original price and reasons for need of a refurbishment?
Battery back up to keep the time if the power goes out? If so, how long can we expect the battery to last before replacement?
[cerealJay] This unit has no battery. The ebay listing is wrong:
"It can be powered by either AC input or batteries"
No it can't.
Further more, the reason these clock radios are obsolete, is even the models that do have battery backup don't work like you'd expect. When mains power goes out, your clock with backup battery will go dark as if powered off. The only function the battery serves is to remember the time, not actually display the time. This hopeless limitation belongs in the past.
[carrawa] I agree it should have a dedicated battery to keep at least the basic functions on like alarm and time, preferably rechargeable.
I was hoping as you described it would at least keep the time even if no display. Annoying to constantly reset everything when the power goes out, the good old days of the Qld power outages.
I remember when those Optus customers only relying on their phones had some early wake up times waiting at train stations for trains that were not coming for hours and quite confused as to why.
[INFIDEL] No it's your misunderstanding of the listing that is wrong!
So not worthy of a NEG VOTE!
This clock is powered by 6V DC.
This can be from the included plug pack OR other 6V source like a battery.
There is no promise of a battery backup!
So "It can be powered by either AC input or batteries" is correct.
[McFly] Sure. They should also write it can be powered by thermoelectric generator or fusion reactor.
[INFIDEL] @McFly: Already states It includes the plug pack needed to drop the voltage from your mythical powerplants to 6V!
So already described in listing.
As I wrote below, have powered a similar 6V DAB+ from old 5V powerbank. Easily rechargeable.
[INFIDEL] Have more than a decade experience with DAB+ & building digital clocks long before that.
Found with other DAB+ clocks, they will usually operate from an ordinary 5V USB powerbank and suitable cable & plug.
Powerbank could be charged from mains power, ensuring an uninterruptible power supply & display if the mains power fails.
DAB+ clocks derive the Internet time signal from the radio.
So a battery backup of time is unnecessary.
As long as they are powered, they display the correct time.
Mains clocks with battery backups merely provide a backup of approximate time from an oscillator, when the 50hz time reference from the mains power is lost. When power resumes, they show approximate time.
Without a battery backup - time, alarms, etc needs to be completely reset manually.
No Mains clocks would likely display the time (even with a battery backup) during a power outage.
Battery operated DAB+ radios have 2 alarms, but usually have tiny displays.
Internet connected clocks & radios are available. Main clock in my home is a big $10 Kmart one. Time, date, etc are derived from Wifi. But no display if power fails.
With mobile phones & apps displaying the accurate time, & able to set multiple alarms - haven't used an alarm clock in many years!!
[The Magic Pudding] The Sangean radio from this deal worked well as a kitchen radio so I'll try this, though DAB is useless here.
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/967528
[huntingforbargainz] Might as well start selling record players.
[liam2040] seems like a cheap way to feed DAB to a slightly older receiver without turning the TV on
[INFIDEL] Feed my $13 Sangean DAB+ earphone socket (stereo) into old stereo. (3.5mm plug to rca stereo cable)
Sounds great at low cost.
[McFly] Yes, pretty rare for something like this to have a line-out.
